scene: Day 164, a frozen white dawn in the packed depot yard. Patch (white round head, orange bandage above his right eye, orange backpack) kneels on the frosty roof of the beige coach at an open square roof hatch, close to the camera, eyes wide in terror, one sweat drop, gripping a long pole that goes down through the hatch. Below in the aisle, the night driver walker (green head, navy-blue two-pocket vest) has both hands clamped on the pole, and a ring of keys dangles from a wire hook at its tip. All around the coach, a sea of frost-covered green walkers stands packed shoulder to shoulder, faces slowly turning up. Beside Patch, Nora (purple band on her forearm) holds out her open mitten hand. Tense because the dead man is winning the tug of war for his own keys.

Day 172, frosty morning beside the coach. Patch hangs head first down the side of the beige coach, upside down, held by the ankles by a figure in a red beanie lying on the coach roof, his orange backpack dangling and his orange bandage close to the camera, eyes huge. In front of his face, a small battery door is open with two thick jump-lead clamps attached. A frost-covered green walker stands a hand's width away from his face, its head halfway through turning toward him, mouth starting to open, with hundreds more packed behind it. Tense because the walker is about to finish turning.
